The database schema named rschema_0041 consists of 8 tables. The tables are described as follows:
1. Property_Manager: This table contains information about property managers. It has columns for Email (a string of up to 255 characters), Name (a string of up to 255 characters), Phone (a string of up to 255 characters), and Property_Manager_ID (an integer) which is the primary key.
2. Repair_Staff: This table contains information about repair staff. It has columns for Name (a string of up to 255 characters), Phone (a string of up to 255 characters), and Repair_Staff_ID (an integer) which is the primary key.
3. Community: This table contains information about communities. It has columns for Community_ID (an integer), Location (a string of up to 255 characters), Name (a string of up to 255 characters), and Property_Manager_ID (an integer) which is a foreign key referencing Property_Manager.
4. Resident: This table contains information about residents. It has columns for Building_ID (an integer), Community_ID (an integer), Email (a string of up to 255 characters), Name (a string of up to 255 characters), Phone (a string of up to 255 characters), and Resident_ID (an integer) which is the primary key. The Community_ID is a foreign key referencing Community.
5. Management: This table serves as a junction table for many-to-many relationship between Property_Manager and Community. It has columns for Community_ID (an integer) and Property_Manager_ID (an integer) which are foreign keys referencing Community and Property_Manager respectively.
6. Repair_Order: This table contains information about repair orders. It has columns for Community_ID (an integer), Repair_Content (a string of up to 255 characters), Repair_Cost (a float), Repair_Date (a datetime), Repair_Order_ID (an integer) which is the primary key, Repair_Staff_ID (an integer) which is a foreign key referencing Repair_Staff, and Resident_ID (an integer) which is a foreign key referencing Resident.
7. Residence: This table serves as a junction table for many-to-many relationship between Resident and Community. It has columns for Building_ID (an integer), Community_ID (an integer), and Resident_ID (an integer) which are foreign keys referencing Community and Resident respectively.
8. Execution: This table serves as a junction table for many-to-many relationship between Repair_Order and Repair_Staff. It has columns for Repair_Order_ID (an integer) and Repair_Staff_ID (an integer) which are foreign keys referencing Repair_Order and Repair_Staff respectively.
All columns allow null values except for those in the Community, Resident, and Management tables where NOT NULL constraints are applied. The primary keys and foreign keys enforce entity integrity and referential integrity in the database.
gold_question:
Business requirement description:
The real estate company manages the property management of multiple communities. Each community has a community number, name, location and property manager. The property manager can manage multiple communities, but each community has only one property manager, and the name, phone number and email address of the property manager need to be recorded. Each community has multiple residents, and each resident has a resident number, name, phone number, email address and building number. Every time the property is repaired, the maintenance order number, community number, resident number, maintenance date, maintenance content, maintenance cost and maintenance personnel information must be recorded. The maintenance personnel information includes the maintenance personnel number, name and phone number.
ddl:
-- Schema for database: rschema_0041
CREATE TABLE `property_manager` (
  `property_manager_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `phone` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`property_manager_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `repair_staff` (
  `repair_staff_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `phone` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`repair_staff_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `community` (
  `community_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `location` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `property_manager_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`community_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `community_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`property_manager_id`) REFERENCES `property_manager` (`property_manager_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `resident` (
  `resident_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `building_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `community_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `phone` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`resident_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `resident_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`community_id`) REFERENCES `community` (`community_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `management` (
  `community_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `property_manager_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`community_id`, `property_manager_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `management_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`community_id`) REFERENCES `community` (`community_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `management_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`property_manager_id`) REFERENCES `property_manager` (`property_manager_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `repair_order` (
  `repair_order_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `community_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `repair_content` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `repair_cost` float DEFAULT NULL,
  `repair_date` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `repair_staff_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `resident_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`repair_order_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `repair_order_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`repair_staff_id`) REFERENCES `repair_staff` (`repair_staff_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `repair_order_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`resident_id`) REFERENCES `resident` (`resident_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `repair_order_ibfk_3` FOREIGN KEY (`community_id`) REFERENCES `community` (`community_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `residence` (
  `building_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `community_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `resident_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`community_id`, `resident_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `residence_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`community_id`) REFERENCES `community` (`community_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `residence_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`resident_id`) REFERENCES `resident` (`resident_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `execution` (
  `repair_order_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `repair_staff_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`repair_order_id`, `repair_staff_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `execution_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`repair_order_id`) REFERENCES `repair_order` (`repair_order_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `execution_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`repair_staff_id`) REFERENCES `repair_staff` (`repair_staff_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
